discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Will J. Percival
nominees.affiliation: University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute, Canada

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Percival et al.) teams independently detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies, a feature at about 150 Mpc set by the physics of the photon-baryon plasma before recombination. This turned galaxy surveys into a geometric probe of cosmic expansion, calibrated by the cosmic microwave background and largely immune to astrophysical systematics. Eisenstein developed the theory of the acoustic scale and the reconstruction technique that sharpens it; Cole and Percival led the 2dFGRS power-spectrum analysis and then built BAO into a precision programme through BOSS and eBOSS. BAO now underpins our measurement of dark energy, independently confirming acceleration, and in 2024-25 DESI BAO results have opened a serious, evidence-based test of whether dark energy is a constant Lambda or evolves with time.
